issue: What standard of appellate review applies to a sufficiency-of-the-evidence challenge that was not preserved by a specific Rule 29 motion: full waiver, a manifest-miscarriage-of-justice or clear-and-gross-injustice standard, or plain error?

sides.position: Full waiver: an unpreserved sufficiency argument is not reviewed at all
cases: United States v. Porter, 886 F.3d at 566

sides.position: Review only for a manifest miscarriage of justice
cases: United States v. Chong Lam, 677 F.3d at 200 n.10
United States v. Graf, 610 F.3d at 1166

sides.position: Review only for clear and gross injustice
cases: United States v. Marston, 694 F.3d at 134
United States v. Samuels, 874 F.3d at 1036
United States v. Baston, 818 F.3d at 664
United States v. Hosseini, 679 F.3d at 550
United States v. Goode, 483 F.3d at 681
United States v. Spinner, 152 F.3d at 955
United States v. Husmann, 765 F.3d 169, 172 (3d Cir. 2014)
United States v. Sussman, 709 F.3d 155, 162 (3d Cir. 2013)
United States v. Williams, 974 F.3d 320 (3d Cir. 2020)

this_court: Plain-error review (the Third Circuit reviews unpreserved sufficiency arguments for plain error)
quote: The circuits are more divided on this question than on the preservation standard itself.
cite: United States v. Jabree Williams, 974 F.3d 320 (3rd Cir. 2020)
